newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end down on lack of pension fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end down on lack of pension fund buying.

text.p: The Seoul bourse ended Tuesday's trading lower as disappointment spread due to a lack of aggressive buying by public pension funds, brokers said.
The composite stock index fell 7.05 points to provisionally close at 677.76. Volume was a thin 23.78 million, while decliners eclipsed advancers 779 to 156.

"The biggest reason for the decline is that pension funds weren't as active as investors had hoped," said a Seoul Securities broker. "Also, many players, especially foreigners, are away on holiday and aren't in the market."
Despite a request by the finance ministry to buy 300 billion won worth of stocks before the year's close, public pension funds have not actively entered the market, brokers said.

An official at the Government Employees Pension Fund said the fund had purchased 10 billion won worth of large-cap and blue-chip shares. However, this was much less than the 30 billion won analysts had predicted the funds would buy daily.

The listing of eight initial public offerings (IPOs) also dampened sentiment. Samsung Engineering and Kukdong City Gas ended limit up, up 3,200 won to 43,200 and 2,800 to 37,800, respectively. But three others fell to their lower limits.
Blue chip KEPCO, one of the market's heaviest weighted stocks, rebounded after falling in recent days. It rose 300 won to 25,100.
The bourse will be closed for trading on Christmas Day.
